Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee.text_block: In the six first days, from Monday to the Saturday of the Prodigal, the Triodion has nothing, but only the Octoechos and Menaion. – Fast-free week.
Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee.header_raw: Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee

Sunday of the Prodigal Son.text_block:
1.	In the five first days, from Monday to Meatfare Friday, the Triodion has nothing, but only the Octoechos and Menaion.
2.	Meatfare Saturday – Soul Saturday.

Meatfare Sunday.text_block:
Of the Last Judgment
1.	The service of Cheesefare Week is penitential, like a Forefeast before Great Lent.
2.	On Monday, Tuesday and Thursday the Triodion has little, the rest is in the Octoechos and Menaion.
3.	On Wednesday and Friday the Triodion has a fuller Lenten service.
4.	Влк: Cheesefare Saturday. To the Holy Ascetics.

Cheesefare Sunday.text_block:
Expulsion of Adam
1.	In the five days, from Monday to Friday of the 1st week of Lent, the service is Lenten. On Monday begins the Great Forty Days.
2.	First Saturday of Great Lent. Great Martyr Theodore the Tyro.

First Sunday of Lent.text_block:
Orthodoxy: Against the Iconoclasts
1.	In the five days, from Monday to Friday of the 2nd week of Lent, the service is Lenten.
2.	From Monday onwards we take at Compline the Canon of the saints of the Menaion falling from the Saturday of Lazarus to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, both inclusive.
3.	Second Saturday of Lent: service to the Martyrs, Hierarchs and All Saints, also for the deceased – according to the rubric of Saturdays with "Alleluia," with the service of the daily saint of the Menaion. Likewise on the 3rd and 4th Saturdays of Lent.

Second Sunday of Lent.text_block:
Without name. Penitential
1.	In the five days, from Monday to Friday of the 3rd week of Lent, the service is Lenten.
2.	Third Saturday of Lent: service of Saturday with "Alleluia" just as on the 2nd Saturday of Lent.

Third Sunday of Lent.text_block:
Veneration of the Cross
1.	In the five days, from Monday to Friday of the 4th week of Lent, the service is of the Veneration of the Cross.
2.	Fourth Saturday of Lent: service as on the 2nd and 3rd Saturdays of Lent.

Fourth Sunday of Lent.text_block:
Without name. Penitential
At choice – also the service of Ven. John Climacus.
1.	On Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday of the 5th week of Lent the service is Lenten.
2.	On Thursday of the 5th week of Lent: penitential service of the Great Canon, with prostrations.
3.	Saturday of the 5th week of Lent – Akathist Saturday.

Fifth Sunday of Lent.text_block:
Without name. Penitential
At choice – also the service of Ven. Mary of Egypt.
In the five days, from Monday to Friday of the 6th week of Lent, the service is Lenten.

Sixth Saturday of Lent – of Lazarus.text_block: Canons of the saints of the Menaion which were taken at Compline from Monday of the 2nd week of Lent onwards, from this Saturday to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas.
Sixth Saturday of Lent – of Lazarus.header_raw: Sixth Saturday of Lent – of Lazarus

Sixth Sunday of Lent – Flower [Palm].text_block:
One-day feast with Vigil
1.	On Great Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday the service is of the Passion and Penitential, as if anticipating Christ's Passion .
2.	On Great Thursday: Mystical Supper and beginning of Christ's Passion.
3.	On Great Friday: Christ's Passion.
4.	On Great Saturday: Burial of Christ in the tomb.

= PASCHA: RESURRECTION OF CHRIST.text_block:
39-day feast
1.	From Monday to Bright Saturday inclusive we sing the entire service to the Resurrection.
2.	On Monday and Tuesday we abstain from work and participate in the divine service.
During the week it is permitted to eat meat.

= SECOND SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA –.text_block:
ANTIPASCHA – OF THOMAS
7-day feast with Vigil
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday in the midst of the feast of Sunday of Ap. Thomas, with the Menaion.

Third Sunday after Pascha – of the Myrrh.text_block:
7-day feast
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday – in the midst of the feast of the Myrrh-bearers, with the Menaion.
Third Sunday after Pascha – of the Myrrh.header_raw: Third Sunday after Pascha – of the Myrrh-bearers

Fourth Sunday after Pascha – of the Para.text_block:
3-day feast
1.	Monday and Tuesday – in the midst of the feast of the Paralytic, with the Menaion.
2.	Wednesday of Mid-Pentecost. 8-day feast, without Vigil and without Polyeleos.
Fourth Sunday after Pascha – of the Para.header_raw: Fourth Sunday after Pascha – of the Paralytic

Fifth Sunday after Pascha – of the Samar.text_block:
4-day feast
1.	Monday and Tuesday – in the midst of the feast of Mid-Pentecost; the service of the Samaritan Woman is delayed until the feast of Mid-Pentecost is given away.
2.	Влк: Wednesday: Apodosis of Mid-Pentecost.
3.	Thursday, Friday and Saturday – in the midst of the feast of the Samaritan Woman.
Fifth Sunday after Pascha – of the Samar.header_raw: Fifth Sunday after Pascha – of the Samaritan Woman

Sixth Sunday after Pascha – of the Blind.text_block:
4-day feast
1.	Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday – in the midst of the feast of the Blind Man; on Wednesday – also Влк: Apodosis of Pascha and Forefeast of Ascension.
2.	Thursday: = ASCENSION. 9-day feast with Vigil.
Sixth Sunday after Pascha – of the Blind.header_raw: Sixth Sunday after Pascha – of the Blind Man

Seventh Sunday after Pascha – of the Hol.text_block:
1.	Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday – in the midst of the feast of Ascension.
2.	Friday: Влк: Apodosis of Ascension.
3.	Soul Saturday. Everything according to the rubric of Meatfare Saturday here, on p. 320.
Seventh Sunday after Pascha – of the Hol.header_raw: Seventh Sunday after Pascha – of the Holy Fathers

SUNDAY OF PENTECOST..text_block:
DESCENT OF THE HOLY SPIRIT
7-day feast with Vigil
1.	Monday of the Holy Spirit (and feast of the Most Holy Trinity – at choice). Abstention from work with presence at divine service.
2.	During the week it is permitted to eat meat.
3.	Saturday: Влк: Apodosis of the Descent of the Holy Spirit.

First Sunday after the Descent of the Ho.text_block:
Here ends the Old Triodion
1.	On this Sunday begins the cycle of Sunday Matins Gospels and daily Liturgy [Gospels/Epistles].
2.	On Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday the Triodion has nothing.
3.	Thursday: = OF THE EUCHARIST. 8-day feast. Vigil is transferred to Sunday.
First Sunday after the Descent of the Ho.header_raw: First Sunday after the Descent of the Holy Spirit – of All Saints

Second Sunday after the Descent of the H.text_block:
Vigil of the Eucharist
1.	With this Sunday begins the cycle of tones.
2.	On Thursday: Влк: Apodosis of the feast of the Eucharist.
3.	On Friday: + Compassion of the Most Holy Theotokos. One-day, Polyeleos feast. Here ends the New Triodion.
Services of the Octoechos
On Sunday: Resurrectional
On Monday: Penitential and to the Angels
On Tuesday: Penitential and to the Forerunner
On Wednesday and Friday: of the Cross and to the Theotokos
On Thursday: to the Apostles and St. Nicholas
On Saturday: to All Saints and the deceased

EXPLANATION OF THE TABLE
1.	The table contains 35 columns of Sundays of the whole year, according to the number of 35 Paschal keys and 35 corresponding Paschal days.
2.	At the top of the table, that is, in its 1st transverse row, all 35 Paschal keys are indicated, under each of which extends a row, or column, of Sundays of the whole year, with the indication of the day of the month within which these Sundays fall, and their dates or names. The names of the months are given outside the column, on the left side, and separated from one another by transverse step-like lines; the day of the month is given in the column, and the number or name of the Sunday – outside the column, on the right side of the table.
3.	In the 7th row are given all 35 days on which the Sunday of the Publican may fall, on which the Triodion begins.
4.	In the 8th row are given in double print all 35 Paschal days, corresponding to the 35 Paschal keys.
5.	In the five rows that are between the Publican and the Paschal keys, are indicated all 35 Sundays that may fall between Theophany and the Publican, that is, the Sunday after Theophany and the four last ordinary ones (29th, 30th, 31st and 32nd). However, since not all these Sundays will always take place, the explanation of which we gave on p. 144 (for this depends on whether Pascha falls earlier or later), between these five Sundays some places may be unfilled, and this means that then the Sundays corresponding to them, indicated on the right side of the table, will not take place. For example, under the Paschal key "A" all places are unfilled; this means that none of these 5 Sundays will be taken, but immediately after Theophany – the Triodion.
6.	Of the Triodion Sundays, we presented only three, that is, the middle one – the Resurrection, and the two extreme ones, that is [Page 250] the Publican and All Saints; the rest of the Sundays that are between them, we do not present, for one can conveniently keep them in memory even without the table, because usually they have proper names and services that correspond to these names.
7.	For the Sundays preceding the Sunday of the Publican, we do not present either the tone or the Sunday Gospel, for they depend on the past Pascha, and therefore one must look for them at the end of the table, within the limits of January and February under the Paschal key of the past Pascha.
8.	Next to some Sundays, Latin letters are printed in double type. This means that then, with the Gospel of this Sunday, another must also be combined, of one of the 10 specific Sundays of the Menaion, presented after the table with the corresponding Latin letters .
9.	After this, if you want to find out which Sundays in a certain year should be taken between Theophany and the Publican, seek first of all the Paschal key of the following Pascha, using Table I or Table II, and under it in Table III you will find these Sundays; only, if the year is leap, follow immediately the next column. And if you prefer to find out which Sunday, tone and Sunday Gospel are to be taken on one of the Sundays after the Descent of the Holy Spirit, then having determined the Paschal key of this year and having gone down its column to the place and day of the Sunday, follow from it along the transverse row to the right side of the table and you will find all this.
10.	Regarding the Apodosis of the Meeting, which we present in the last row of the table, know that under the key "A" the number "0" means that the Apodosis will not be then; under keys from "R" to the end, the number "9" means that the Apodosis will be on February 9, and under others – it will be on different days, depending on the keys; only in a leap year follow immediately the next column. Paschal keys must be determined from the following Pascha.
RUBRIC
ABOUT THE HOLY DOORS AND THE CURTAIN OF THE ICONOSTASIS
According to the rubric of the Greek Euchologion, the holy doors are opened only εις την αρχήν του μεγάλου Εσπερινού, οτε θυμια μονός ο Ιερεύς, εις τας εισόδους πασάς, ήγουν των Εσπερινών και της Λειτουργίας, και του αγίου Ευαγγελίου. Ωσαύτως ανοίγεται και από του Μετά φόβου... μέχρι της συμπληρώσεως της θείας Λειτουργίας.
The curtain, according to the present custom of Athonite monasteries, at the Liturgy, after the completion of the Proskomedia, is drawn open, and at the "Great Entrance" is drawn shut; at "Especially" it is drawn open, and at "And grant that with one mouth" it is drawn shut; at "With fear" it is drawn open and so remains until the conclusion of the Liturgy . According to the former custom of the Athonite Mountain, when one priest serves, that is without a deacon, the curtain is drawn shut at the "Great Entrance" and is not drawn open until the end of communion. Besides this, it remains drawn open at Vespers and at Matins from the 1st Hour and at the Moleben. When the Hours are celebrated without Liturgy, it is drawn open for the reading of the Apostle and drawn shut after the dismissal of the "Typika" .
The End and Glory to God.
Bless, O All-Holy Theotokos, this work for the good of God's holy Churches. Amen.
